Run steps in order as one arm

Source: R/core-compose-step.R
hr_chain.Rd

hr_chain() turns steps into an hr_arm() whose run passes the item to the first step, what that returns to the second, and so on, and returns what the last step returns. Each step is called as step(x, ctx), where ctx is the arm's context with ctx$step (the step's name) and ctx$step_params (its resolved settings) added; ctx$params stays the arm's params.

Usage

hr_chain(..., name, version = "0.0.1")

Arguments

...

Steps, or a chain to derive from followed by steps and NULLs.

name

The chain's name, one string, as an arm's name.

version

The chain's version, one string.

Value

An hr_arm() with the attribute hr_steps, the named list of its steps in order.

Details

Steps come from hr_step(), gr_step() or gr_step_retrieve(). A named argument names its step, and the name is written into the step; an unnamed one keeps the step's own name. Names must be unique, must not contain a dot (a setting is named "step.setting") and must not be name or version.

Given a chain first, hr_chain() derives a new chain from it: x = NULL drops step x, x = step replaces step x where it stands, and a step under a new name is added at the end. So hr_chain(checked, judge = NULL, name = "nojudge") is checked without its judge.

The order is checked when the chain is built, from what each step declares it takes and returns. A step that takes "chunks" when no step before it returns chunks warns with class hr_chain_gap: a gr_step() read step would cut the document at the default settings without saying so. A step that takes "doc" with no step before it returning one does not warn: a chain usually starts at the segment step, which reads the document at the default ingest settings, and a warning there would fire on almost every chain. Add an ingest step first to choose those settings. After a step that returns "answer", only steps that take "answer" or "state", or declare nothing, may follow; any other is an error of class hr_bad_chain. A held command step (see hr_step_command()) must come last, or be followed only by other held steps; any other step after it is an error of class hr_held_not_last.

The arm records each step's settings as given, as "step.setting", in params and as the settings hr_benchmark() turns into param.* columns. Its configuration, which hr_sweep() and hr_benchmark() compare, is a hash of the steps' names, versions, code, the values that code reads and the resolved settings, so a setting given at its default gives the same configuration as the setting left out. hr_settings() lists every setting of the chain by path, hr_set() changes some of them, and hr_sweep() sweeps them by path, as hr_sweep(chain, data.frame(retrieve.top_k = c(2, 8))).

See also

hr_step(), gr_step(), hr_settings(), hr_set(), hr_benchmark(), vignette("compose")

Other harness: gr_arm(), gr_condensation_check(), gr_qa_reference(), gr_reverse_text(), gr_scorer_answer(), hr_arm(), hr_benchmark(), hr_contrast(), hr_drift_check(), hr_effort_check(), hr_effort_escalate(), hr_effort_event(), hr_effort_log(), hr_mdd(), hr_modules(), hr_reference(), hr_register(), hr_report(), hr_scorer(), hr_set(), hr_settings(), hr_skill(), hr_step(), hr_step_command(), hr_sweep(), hr_sweep_check()

Examples

cl <- hr_mock_client(function(m, p) "Revenue was 45.2 million dollars.")
ref <- gr_qa_reference(
  questions = c(revenue = "What was revenue in 2024?"),
  documents = gr_example(), answers = list("45.2 million"), split = "test")
tidy <- hr_step("tidy", function(a, ctx) {
  a$answer <- trimws(a$answer)
  a
}, input = "answer", output = "answer")
checked <- hr_chain(segment = gr_step("segment"),
                    retrieve = gr_step_retrieve(top_k = 4),
                    read = gr_step("read", reader = "stuff"),
                    tidy = tidy, name = "checked")
plain <- hr_chain(checked, tidy = NULL, name = "plain")
names(attr(plain, "hr_steps"))
#> [1] "segment"  "retrieve" "read"    
old <- hr_options(verbose = FALSE)
bench <- hr_benchmark(list(checked, plain), ref, runs = 5, client = cl,
                      scorer = gr_scorer_answer())
table(bench$arm, bench$correct)
#>          
#>           TRUE
#>   checked    5
#>   plain      5
hr_options(old)
